newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IMPLATS SAYS OUTPUT UNAFFECTED BY STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: IMPLATS SAYS OUTPUT UNAFFECTED BY STRIKE.

text.p: Impala Platinum Ltd (Implats) said on Thursday production at its platinum refineries were unaffected by a three-day strike over wages by workers.
Implats spokeswoman Marilyn Watson said striking workers had moved away from access gates to the refineries which prevented deliveries of feed stock on Wednesday.
She said the strike was continuing with no settlement reached yet but said production had not been affected.
"We have had people in both refineries to keep production going," Watson said, adding that the refineries were operating at full production levels.
Implats said on Wednesday it had evicted some 100 striking workers who staged a sit-in protest.

Implats said its refineries' management was taking steps to try to ensure compliance with the Labour Court order it was granted on Tuesday which directed strikers not to hamper normal operations or threaten other workers.
Around 400 members of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM), out of the 1,100 workforce, embarked on strike action on August 4.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, against the NUM's last demand of 19.2 percent.
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996.
